Issued at 125 PM EDT Mon Sep 28 2026

As high pressure ridging leaves the Upper Great Lakes this afternoon 
through tonight, expect mostly sunny skies across the area to allow 
highs to reach into the mid-70s across much of the area once again, 
allowing for pleasant early-Fall weather to complement the gorgeous 
Fall colors across the Yoop. Heading into the overnight hours, 
expect the mostly clear skies to continue, allowing the temperatures 
to tank down to the dewpoint once again and creating areas of fog; 
could see the need for a Dense Fog Advisory for portions of the 
interior U.P. tonight into Tuesday morning given that visibilities 
could become a quarter mile or less, but confidence on the timing of 
the fog and where it will be dense (quarter mile or less vis) at is 
too low at this point in time to issue Special Weather Statements or 
Dense Fog Advisories. Nevertheless, the greatest chances for dense 
fog do look to be in the east half tonight as some upper-level cloud 
cover begins to move into the western U.P. by the early morning 
hours; expect lows around 50 in the west to the 40s and potentially 
even mid-30s over the interior east tonight. 

Attention then turns to troughing over the central CONUS on Tuesday 
that develops split flow, with one low moving through Canada towards 
Hudson Bay while another forms in the Southern Plains before lifting 
and dissipating northeastward towards the Mid-Atlantic/New England 
through the mid to late-week period. With this in mind, a preceding 
shortwave low lifts from the Northern Plains towards Hudson Bay on 
Tuesday, bringing upper-level cloud cover across the area. 
Nevertheless, expect another pleasantly warm Fall day on Tuesday, 
with the U.P. perhaps being set up with some light rain showers late 
Tuesday into Wednesday as the shortwave passes along the periphery 
of our area. While the 850mb LLJ increases up to 35 to 45 kts aloft 
Tuesday afternoon and evening with the passage of the shortwave low, 
no severe weather or even breezy conditions are expected as there 
will be very little to no instability to work with aloft and capping 
is expected just above the sfc due to subtle WAA creating a stable 
atmospheric profile in the lower levels. While the low that develops 
over the Southern Plains and lifts towards the Mid-Atlantic/New 
England could bring additional light rain showers to the area 
Wednesday into Thursday, more medium range guidance does suggest a 
more southerly track to the precipitation chances, with now only the 
south central and east perhaps seeing synoptic rainfall, if even 
that. That being said, once the cold sector moves through, expect 
winds to pick up from the west to northwest across the area late 
Wednesday night and Thursday; while the temperature advection and 
height rises do weaken with time on Thursday, we could see wind 
gusts of 30 to potentially even 40 mph along the Lake Superior 
shoreline on Thursday. In addition, the delta-Ts and winds over Lake 
Superior may be enough to kick-off some quick-hitting lake/upslope-
induced light rain/drizzle showers over the northwest wind belts 
before ending by Thursday evening. Overall, rain totals continue to 
decrease with this event, with expected amounts now around a tenth 
to quarter inch for most of the west and north central. While the 
south central and east could see around half an inch of rainfall or 
more, only the area near Menominee now looks to receive an inch or 
more of rainfall, with the NBM now only showing up to a 50% chance 
of that happening. 

Moving into the rest of the week into this upcoming weekend, expect 
more normal Fall temperatures as highs are projected to only rise up 
into the lower 60s during the afternoon hours from Thursday onward. 
With high pressure redeveloping over the Northern Plains for the 
latter portion of the week behind the troughing and potential 
rainfall, expect fairly pleasant Fall weather to continue until rain 
chances potentially return with a Clipper low this weekend. Given 
the fairly clear skies expected with the ridging moving through late 
this week, we may see some widespread frost develop over the 
interior areas Thursday and Friday nights; keep an eye on the 
forecast to see the latest updates.
